rationale: Dispatches the case built to separate the sweep's two candidate conditions, after a local run that already changes how I read the confound. The case polls the origin's decided index for up to thirty seconds before re-electing it, so the re-synchronisation is known to have completed if it completes at all; locally it did not: `resync_completed_before_reelection` false after a 30.1 s wait, the origin's decided index still 0, and the shift still delivered (`resolved` ok with index 3 while entry 33 sits at index 1 and the decided log is 33,34,35). That means the sweep's phase field does not distinguish the two candidate conditions at all - at this construction the field never flips to 1 no matter how long one waits, so the earlier 'confound' reading was based on a field that is not a proxy for the ordering I thought it measured. I am recording that correction rather than keeping the confound as a live explanation. What the field does show is that in this construction the origin is never re-synchronised before it is re-elected, at any tick period, and the shift appears only at the two larger tick periods, which restores the tick period as the better-supported condition while leaving the precise mechanism of the stale placeholders unobserved.

investigations.discriminator: Pending the submitted case's receipt. The separation attempt already shows locally that `decided_after_resync` is not a proxy for the ordering between re-synchronisation and re-election at this construction (it stays 0 after a thirty-second wait), so the sweep's apparent confound was a reading error on my side rather than a second live condition. Remaining open: why the origin's decided index never advances in this scenario, and whether the stale placeholders that shift the reported index come from the batch flush or from the truncation.

scope.description: One run of the same lost-entry scenario at a 1000 ms tick period, with one difference: instead of sleeping a fixed multiple of the tick period after restoring the links, the harness polls the origin's decided index every 500 ms for up to thirty seconds, records how long it waited and whether the index had advanced, and only then re-elects the origin and buffers the fresh entry. The run reports the same quantities as the sweep plus the wait and whether the re-synchronisation was observed to complete before the re-election.
assumptions: Polling the origin's decided index is a valid way to detect that its re-synchronisation completed, because that index only advances through messages from a leader it has promised.

The scenario, batch size (3), election and resend tick counts, cut-off and re-election steps are identical to the sweep cases, so a difference in outcome is attributable to the wait rather than to the construction.
A thirty-second bound is long compared with the resend interval (two tick periods), so a completion that this design can produce should occur inside it.
No target logic is modified; the harness only chooses when to re-elect.
excluded: Any claim that the origin's decided index cannot advance in other constructions; only this one was run.
Any claim about the internal placeholder queue, which is not observable through the public API.
Any claim about tick periods other than 1000 ms in this case.

experiment.prefix: Build three actors with batch_size 3 and a 1000 ms tick period, node 1 carrying leader_priority 1. Elect node 1 and emit the admission event. Buffer `append_notify(11)` and `append_notify(12)` on node 1 so both are deferred into its batch. Block node 1's links to nodes 2 and 3 both ways, wait until nodes 2 and 3 report node 3 as the accepted leader, and call `append_notify(22)` on it. Unblock the links, then poll node 1's decided index every 500 ms for up to thirty seconds, recording the wait and whether the index had advanced, before calling `try_become_leader()` on node 1 until it reports itself as the accepted leader. Spawn `append_notify(33)` on node 1, follow with plain appends 34 and 35, sleep several ticks, and await the fresh call. Read node 1's decided suffix, find the 1-based position of entry 33 and the entry at the returned index, and emit the outcome event with the resolution, the returned index, the true position, whether they agree, the entry at the returned index, the decided values, the poll wait and whether the re-synchronisation was observed to complete.
semantic_changes: One case added that polls the origin's re-synchronisation to a bound before re-electing it, plus the wait and completion fields on every case's outcome event.
experiment.responsibility: The decisive inputs come from the target: the origin's decided index only advances through messages from a leader it has promised, batching defers the writes into `unconfirmed_local`, and `reconcile_unconfirmed` maps queued placeholders to index advances to compute what it reports. The harness only chooses when to re-elect and reads the endpoints.

comparisons.description: If the fresh call resolves Ok, the returned index must be the entry's true position. Locally this was violated even after the thirty-second poll, so a violation is expected; a correct index here would show the wait changes the outcome.

experiment.revision_reason: Adds one separation case and the measurement it needs: `run_shift_case` takes a flag that, when set, polls the origin's decided index (up to thirty seconds, 500 ms steps) before the re-election instead of sleeping a fixed multiple of the tick period, and every case now also reports the wait and whether the origin had observed a decided index by then. The existing cases and their constructions are unchanged; a fresh execution is required because the harness bytes changed.
